import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Ensure column names are stripped of any leading/trailing whitespace
df.columns = df.columns.str.strip()

# Filter for the most recent year in the dataset for a current snapshot
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest_year = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year].copy()

# Aggregate data: count dogs per district and gender
# Since 'AnzHunde' column in the sample rows is 1, counting rows (.size())
# effectively counts individual dog registrations.
dog_counts = df_latest_year.groupby(['KreisLang', 'SexHundLang']).size().reset_index(name='NumDogs')

# Sort districts by the total number of dogs for better readability of the plot
total_dogs_per_kreis = dog_counts.groupby('KreisLang')['NumDogs'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
ordered_kreise = total_dogs_per_kreis.index

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))

# Create a grouped bar plot to show the number of dogs by district and gender
sns.barplot(
    data=dog_counts,
    x='KreisLang',
    y='NumDogs',
    hue='SexHundLang',
    order=ordered_kreise,  # Apply the sorting to the x-axis
    palette='viridis'
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title(f'Number of Dog Registrations by District and Gender in Zurich ({latest_year})', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('District (Kreis)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Number of Dog Registrations', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels to prevent overlap and improve readability
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')

# Place the legend outside the plot area to avoid obstructing the bars
plt.legend(title='Dog Gender', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left')

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust layout to ensure all elements (labels, title, legend) fit within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
